subject.title: Config: scaffold compaction loop guard settings

question: Should OpenClaw publish `agents.defaults.compaction.guard` as the future saturated-session compaction guard namespace, or should this work build on the existing `tools.loopDetection.postCompactionGuard` and canonical issue design instead?
rationale: The patch is focused, but it adds a public config/default surface before maintainer agreement on compaction-loop guard ownership, defaults, and reset-recommendation policy.

options.title: Defer To Canonical Issue
options.body: Keep the PR open but paused while maintainers decide the namespace, defaults, and runtime semantics in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/48238.

options.title: Adopt This Namespace
options.body: Accept the new config surface after the contributor rebases, adds upgrade-proofed docs/tests, and explains how it coexists with or supersedes `tools.loopDetection.postCompactionGuard`.

options.title: Close And Redesign
options.body: Close this branch if maintainers decide the separate `agents.defaults.compaction.guard` namespace should not become public config.

recommendation.title: Defer To Canonical Issue
recommendation.body: Keep the PR open but paused while maintainers decide the namespace, defaults, and runtime semantics in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/48238.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent history across compaction safeguard schema and post-compaction guard policy work.
